Below that, one column of running text with a decorative initial at the start of the first paragraph. A rule divides the text from the next section, which has a centred heading "INTENTIO I.", a centred title "Qua doctrina de orbibus cœlestibus examinatur.", the heading "ARTICVLVS. main_text.l: DE COELO
LIBRI DVO.
Liber Primus.
Tractatum de Cœlo, etsi rei difficul-
tas contrarium suadebat, dignitas ta-
men, ordoque naturæ ut de nobilissi-
ma mundi parte, præcipuoque, atque
universali Naturæ organo principem
fecit, qui reliquarum mundi partium, earumque
partuum inspectionem anteeat. In quo quidem opere
non tam animus est, aut spes, quæ sunt certa proferre,
quam quæ parum probabiliter Aristoteles hac de
re philosophatus est, breviter examinare, deinde
Antiquorum sententias cum ipsius dogmate comparare;
tum aliquid de nostro, quod tamen ab Anti-
quorum principiis non abhorreat, apponere quod
& admirationem, ni fallor, & oblectationem excitet
in animis Philosophorum, vel saltem talem opinio-
nem, ut si minus nobis assentiantur, non certè im-
probent hanc operam: in qua si nova videbunt, pulchra
tamen, quæque rationis limites non excedant.
INTENTIO I.
Qua doctrina de orbibus cœlestibus
examinatur.

page.notes: The decorative initial at the start of the first paragraph is read as T ("Tractatum"); it is ornate and could be misread, so the word is not marked with [?] but should be checked. The initial of the last paragraph is read as O ("ORdiamur"). "partuum" in "earumque partuum" is printed as it stands and appears to be a printing error for "partium". "assentiantur" is read from "affentiantur" with the long s rendered as s. The catchword "cœ-" is at the right foot below the last line and is the start of the next word. Stray marks on the left and right margins are not printed text and were left out.
